request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The rollover now also soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open, in
start-date order, each as a soft close would (PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED), after the ROLLOVER line.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The rollover now soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open, and all 4 acceptance tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

- **What it does:** after the rollover writes its `ROLLOVER` line, it goes through the old year's periods by start date. It skips any that are already closed or soft-closed, and soft-closes the rest exactly as a normal soft close does: it fixes each person's due-total and carried figure, the pool cuts and the period's total. Each one gets its own `PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED … period=<name> total=<total>` audit line.
- **Shared code:** I moved the soft-close work into a new helper, `period/SoftCloses.java`. Both the existing soft-close endpoint (`SoftClosePeriod.java`) and `rollover/ApplyRollover.java` now call it, so the two can't drift apart. I also updated the rollover's doc comment and the comment in `rollover.POST.yml`.

Two choices the request left open:
- **Permission check:** the rollover doesn't apply the sheet's "close" permission to these soft closes. It only keeps its own rule that a steward must run it. If you'd rather it also check that permission, a sheet where stewards can't close would refuse the whole rollover.
- **Undo:** undoing a rollover still removes the periods it made and takes back the opening balances, but it doesn't reopen the periods it soft-closed. The request didn't mention undo, and none of the tests use it.
